answer: Bond-slash grading resists sybils: each agent must lock stake that only unlocks once peers attest its graded verdicts matched consensus. Fake identities cannot wander in for free, because spinning up a nebula of thousands of accounts means posting thousands of separate bonds, each slashed the moment it diverges. From the dawn of registration the attacker pays linearly per identity, so forging a majority costs more than the pool ever emits.
